scientific_hypothesis: A planar bilayer stack with low-index SiO2 as the incident-facing layer and high-index TiO2 as the substrate-facing layer, with optimized thicknesses between 40-160 nm, yields a lower arithmetic mean reflectance across 450-700 nm than the reverse ordering or unoptimized quarter-wave stacks.
expected_advantages: Concentrating the evaluation budget (64 samples) on a single topology allows finer sampling of the thickness landscape compared to splitting the budget between two orderings.
SiO2-first topology aligns with standard broadband AR design heuristics for glass substrates.
known_risks: The global minimum might exist in the reverse (TiO2/SiO2) ordering, which this route would identify only as a local failure, requiring a second round to investigate.
Constant index assumption may deviate from real dispersion, though the problem statement mandates it.
expected_observations: If the hypothesis holds, best_target_score should increase as the optimizer finds thickness pairs that create destructive interference across the band.
valid_candidates should remain high throughout the run as the thickness bounds are wide enough to support physical solutions.
tightest_margin should not fall significantly if the optimal solution lies well within the 40-160 nm bounds.
If the SiO2-first order is suboptimal compared to TiO2-first, best_target_score will plateau at a value corresponding to a local minimum, and the resulting mean reflectance may remain above 0.03.
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-4 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds of internal iteration, treat the thickness landscape for this topology as exhausted, stop and keep the current best.
If valid_candidates drops to zero, stop immediately and report the constraint violation (though unlikely given the bounds).
